metadata.name: Erasmus GBS Respiratory Insufficiency Score (EGRIS)
when_to_use: Calculated at hospital admission in patients with Guillain-Barré syndrome to estimate 1-week mechanical ventilation risk.
next_steps: Patients with EGRIS >= 5 (or declining FVC < 20 mL/kg / NIF > -30 cmH2O) require ICU admission and preparation for early elective intubation.
metadata.summary: 3-item admission score (0–7) predicting the probability of requiring mechanical ventilation within the first week in Guillain-Barré syndrome.
clinical_pearls: Calculate at hospital admission using MRC Sum Score (0–60), presence of facial/bulbar weakness, and days from weakness onset.
Even in low-risk patients, serial bedside FVC / NIF monitoring remains essential if clinical progression continues.
Externally validated across international IGOS regions (Doets et al., 2022), confirming strong overall discrimination for 1-week mechanical ventilation.

Pitfall — Regional calibration & admission-only scope: Absolute predicted probabilities can vary across geographic regions (requiring local calibration), and EGRIS does not replace dynamic respiratory monitoring (FVC < 20 mL/kg, NIF > -30 cmH2O) during hospitalization.

items.label: Days Between Onset of Weakness and Hospital Admission
Facial and/or Bulbar Weakness at Admission

options.label: Present (facial palsy, dysphagia, dysarthria, or weak cough)

items.label: MRC Sum Score at Admission (0–60)
items.subtitle: Sum of 6 bilateral muscle groups (0–5 each)

interpretation.label: Low Risk (0–2 pts · ~4% Ventilation Risk)
interpretation.summary: Low probability (~4%) of mechanical ventilation within 1 week; monitor on neurology ward with regular respiratory checks.

interpretation.label: Intermediate Risk (3–4 pts · ~24% Ventilation Risk)
interpretation.summary: Intermediate probability (~24%) of mechanical ventilation within 1 week; consider step-down/ICU monitoring and frequent FVC/NIF.

interpretation.label: High Risk (5–7 pts · ~65% Ventilation Risk)
interpretation.summary: High probability (~65%) of mechanical ventilation within 1 week; admit to ICU and prepare for early elective intubation if FVC < 20 mL/kg or NIF > -30 cmH2O.

assessment_guides.title: Calculating Admission MRC Sum Score
bedside_steps: Score 6 bilateral muscle pairs (0–5 each): shoulder abduction, elbow flexion, wrist extension, hip flexion, knee extension, ankle dorsiflexion.
Use the NeuroCalc 'MRC Sum Score' calculator if you need to sum all 12 individual muscle groups.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Rapidly progressive weakness (<= 3 days from onset to admission) is a major independent predictor of respiratory failure.

references.citation: Walgaard C, Lingsma HF, Ruts L, et al. Prediction of respiratory insufficiency in Guillain-Barré syndrome. Ann Neurol. 2010;67(6):781-787.
Doets AY, Walgaard C, Lingsma HF, et al. International Validation of the Erasmus Guillain-Barré Syndrome Respiratory Insufficiency Score. Ann Neurol. 2022;91(4):521-531.
